analysis.title: Gold ETF Commentary | October 2026
key_insights: Global physically-backed gold ETFs attracted US$2.7bn in October, the fourth consecutive monthly inflow. Europe led with US$1.8bn, Asia added US$1.3bn, and North America saw outflows of US$512mn.
Global gold ETF holdings rose 19t to a month-end record 4,275t. AUM fell 6% to US$542bn because the lower gold price outweighed inflows.

Year to date, global gold ETFs added US$41bn (holdings +246t), the third strongest on record. Europe accounted for 44% and Asia 45% of net inflows. The UK had the largest country inflows and China was a close second.

North America was the only region with outflows in October (-US$512mn), driven entirely by US-domiciled funds. Canadian funds kept attracting inflows. The report says AI capex worries and a US tech equity sell-off may have led some investors to sell gold holdings for liquidity.

US Treasuries had their strongest monthly return since December 2023 in October, pulling yields down from the highest in nearly 25 years. The report says this and a less aggressive Fed repricing may have diverted investors from gold. US gold ETFs still saw mild net inflows in the last week of October when US equities fell again, which the report links to diversification against midterm election uncertainty and fiscal concerns.

Europe has had net gold ETF inflows for 18 consecutive weeks despite gold price weakness, surging regional yields and shifting central bank expectations. The report reads this as increasingly strategic demand tied to political and fiscal uncertainty in France, the UK and Germany.

Asian investors bought US$1.3bn, a fourth consecutive month of inflows, led by China. Japan and India also saw inflows. Japan's flows coincided with a Nikkei pullback and falling JGB yields. The BoJ left rates unchanged in late October. Indian mutual funds temporarily suspended new subscriptions to gold fund of funds in mid-October, but ETF buying continued.

Global gold market trading volumes fell 13% in October to an average of US$365bn per day. OTC volumes fell 2% to US$219bn/day. LBMA volumes were US$196bn/day, against a 2025 average of US$161bn/day. Exchange-traded volumes fell 25% to US$140bn/day, with COMEX down 22% and Shanghai down 31%. Gold ETF liquidity averaged US$6bn/day, down 20% m/m.

Total COMEX gold net longs fell 94t in October to 560t, the lowest since end-July. Managed money net longs fell 53t, other reportables fell 54t and spreads fell 13t. COMEX gold options net open interest rose 6% in the month and kept rising in the last days of October despite the equity sell-off, possibly from rollovers and dip buying.
SPDR Gold MiniShares Trust had the largest October inflow (US$905.3mn). SPDR Gold Shares (GLD) had the largest outflow (-US$1,761.7mn), followed by iShares Gold Trust (-US$176.3mn).

macro_indicators.reading: Highest since 4 April 2002, reached on 7 October 2026
macro_indicators.interpretation: Yields then fell as equity sell-offs drove safe-haven buying of Treasuries. October was their strongest monthly return since December 2023, which may have diverted flows from gold.

macro_indicators.reading: Unchanged at the late October meeting
macro_indicators.interpretation: Expectations of less aggressive BoJ tightening and lower JGB yields reduced the opportunity cost of holding gold for Japanese investors.
Narrowing headroom, elevated yields and energy shocks raised UK fiscal concerns, which the report links to gold ETF demand.

tension_points.bull_case: European and Asian investors keep buying gold ETFs for diversification against political and fiscal uncertainty. Europe has had 18 straight weeks of inflows despite weaker gold prices. Falling Asian bond yields lower the opportunity cost of holding gold. US ETFs saw mild inflows in the last week of October.
tension_points.bear_case: North American funds had outflows as investors may have sold gold for liquidity during the tech sell-off. Strong Treasury returns and a less aggressive Fed repricing may have diverted flows from gold. COMEX net longs fell to the lowest since end-July and exchange-traded volumes dropped 25%.

theme_stances.key_argument: Persistent European inflows suggest gold ETF demand is increasingly strategic, reflecting political and fiscal uncertainty.
theme_stances.evidence: demand for gold ETFs may be increasingly strategic
